The labels of the three sectors of the inner circle are respectively 1 on the left, 2 on the right, and 2 below; the labels of the three corresponding regions of the outer annulus are respectively 2 on the left, 1 on the right, and 1 below. Then reason: The radius of the outer circle is 6, and the total area is 36π; the radius of the inner circle is 3, and the area is 9π. The three sectors of the inner circle have equal areas, so the area of each inner sector is 9π/3 = 3π. The area of the outer annulus is 36π - 9π = 27π, and the three annular sectors have equal areas, so each area is 27π/3 = 9π. The regions scoring an odd number on a single throw include one sector labeled 1 in the inner circle and two sectors labeled 1 in the outer ring, with total area 3π + 2·9π = 21π. Therefore the probability of getting an odd number with one dart is p = 21π/36π = 7/12, and the probability of getting an even number is q = 5/12. The total score of two darts is odd if and only if one dart is odd and one dart is even, so the probability is 2pq = 2·(7/12)·(5/12) = 35/72.
